decisions.evidence: In rav2 the crop ends just below the baseline of כי רב, so any vowel under the resh is cut off. In the full s50-2 line 1 I can make out the dagesh in the kaf of כי, but at that resolution I can't clearly see a pataḥ under the resh of רב. The image doesn't contradict the primary's pataḥ, but it doesn't confirm it either.

The gav crop is mis-targeted: it shows שמאהבתך, not this phrase. In the full s50-2, line 6 starts עַל, then a short word with a pataḥ under it that's about two letters wide (gimel or nun shape plus bet), joined by a maqaf to הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. I see no yod between the bet and the maqaf, and no tsere under the bet. This disagrees with the primary's reading (yod, tsere/dagesh on the bet).

In the full s50-2 line 7 there's a visible horizontal stroke at the top-line level between ששמחת and בו, the same shape as the other maqafs on the page (מן־הבהמה, אֶת־, גב־). This disagrees with the primary's 'no maqaf'.

In the tight-leolam crop the bet has a dagesh, and the samekh seems to have tsere with a dagesh, which supports the primary on the samekh. The mark under the bet is small and blurred, and I can't tell a pataḥ from a sheva.
The beritekha crop and the full image both show it clearly. The second bet has no dagesh.
The lo crop is clear: holam male on לו, dagesh and sheva under the bet, pataḥ under the he.
The yeshuah2 crop shows a maqaf after מה, a dagesh in the yod, and qamats/tsere under ישועתנו.

decisions.evidence: The ben2 crop is clear: tsere and dagesh in בֵּין.
The einai crop shows tsere under the mem, pataḥ/sheva under the next letters, a dagesh in the final pe, and qamats.
The bizayon2 crop shows a dagesh in the bet, qamats under the zayin, and a holam dot above. The hiriq under the bet looks merged with the qamats mark and isn't fully distinct.
No s51 image was provided, and /tmp/hashachar-s51.png doesn't exist, so I couldn't look at that line. I withdraw my earlier 'everyday' claim as unverified.
